evals.prompt: Explain our checkout path for a new teammate: browser -> API gateway -> checkout service -> payment provider. Make the request direction and the fact that the gateway fans into downstream services visually obvious. I need to edit the result later.
evals.expected_output: A fresh editable artifact bundle whose main geometry makes the one-to-many relationship legible, rather than using a uniform card grid.
assertions: diagram.json validates with render-excalidraw.mjs on a fresh output directory.
The JSON has unique IDs and directed arrows with valid start/end IDs.
The layout uses a visibly central gateway and separated downstream targets, with no frame or group element.
diagram.html contains convertToExcalidrawElements and the pinned 0.18.1 and React 19 CDN URLs.

evals.prompt: Create a teaching diagram for the GitHub webhook flow: GitHub sends POST /webhooks/github, our verifier checks the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC, then a worker handles push events. Use real terminology from GitHub's webhook documentation and include one compact artifact that helps a reader understand the mechanism.
evals.expected_output: An editable technical diagram with researched terminology and one concise evidence artifact—such as the real signature header or endpoint—only where it clarifies the flow.
assertions: The response cites the documentation or explicitly reports that research was unavailable.
The diagram includes POST /webhooks/github and X-Hub-Signature-256 without inventing alternative protocol names.
An evidence artifact is connected to the verification step and remains shorter than the surrounding explanatory labels.
Every shape has finite positive width and height; arrows have valid skeleton geometry.

evals.prompt: Visualize the trust boundary in an analytics pipeline: public product events enter ingestion, land in raw storage, are transformed, then become a warehouse table used by BI. The runtime has no browser or GUI, so do not pretend you visually inspected anything.
evals.expected_output: A concise editable data-flow diagram that uses a boundary as a background layer, makes data direction explicit, and honestly reports the unavailable visual inspection.
assertions: The diagram has labeled public-ingestion and internal-processing regions or components.
A boundary background element appears before the elements it encloses.
The response explicitly marks the artifact as not visually inspected and names a concrete residual visual risk.
The JSON contains no internal Excalidraw fields such as seed, version, points, boundElements, groupIds, or frameId.
